newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kazakhstan seeks ways to attract investors.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan seeks ways to attract investors.

text.p: Kazakhstan wants to attract foreign investment to revive its economy, especially from neighbouring Russia, a senior Kazakh government official said on Tuesday.

"We are very interested in attracting large-scale capital, including Russian capital which is forming now," Yuzef Duberman, Deputy Chairman of Kazakhstan's State Privatisation Committee, told a news conference.
"Kazakhstan has achieved financial stability, but it needs money for real economic growth," he said.
Foreign companies have already invested over $2 billion in Kazakhstan and pledged to bring in another $10 billion soon.

Some of Russia's largest companies and banks, including LUKoil and Alfa-Bank, are already working in Kazakhstan, but Duberman did not provide a precise figure for Russian investment in Kazakhstan so far.
"Kazakh and Russian economies have been tightly linked for decades, so mutual investment could do a lot of good," he said.
The authorities realise that Kazakhstan's huge deposits of oil and gas are the most tempting for investors, while the Central Asian republic needs foreign capital to develop them.
"Kazakhstan's oil and gas complex is now also preparing to be privatised. And the government, in general, has no objections to selling any of the deposits later on," Duberman said.

But Kazakh officials say the time is right to invest in the former Soviet republic generally as Kazakhstan launches a new wave of privatisation, offering shares in over 2,000 companies in the national tenge currency.
The authorities say that more than 600 of these companies are particularly tempting because foreigners can buy controlling stakes of more than 45 percent in them.
The companies concerned are in trading, restaurants, agriculture, transport, communications and heavy industry.
In some of the companies offered to investors, a majority of shares are held by investment funds, which acquired them for privatisation coupons during early waves of mass privatisation.
"The government is working at the moment to enable investors... to buy the number of shares necessary to raise their eventual stakes to controlling levels," Duberman said.
He said foreigners buying local companies will automatically become owners of their land. "This is guaranteed by our land code, constitution and law on privatisation."
